entities.summary: The Treaty of Adrianople concluded the Russo-Turkish War of 1828–29, between Imperial Russia and the Ottoman Empire. The terms favored Russia, which gained access to the mouths of the Danube and new territory on the Black Sea. The treaty opened the Dardanelles to all commercial vessels, granted autonomy to Serbia, and promised autonomy for Greece. It also allowed Russia to occupy Moldavia and Walachia until the Ottoman Empire had paid a large indemnity; those indemnities were later reduced. The treaty was signed on 14 September 1829 in Adrianople by Count Alexey Fyodorovich Orlov of Russia and Abdülkadir Bey of the Ottoman Empire.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Treaty of Adrianople had significant regional impact by granting autonomy to Serbia and promising autonomy for Greece, shaping the modern nation-states in the Balkans. The treaty also marked a shift in the balance of power between Russia and the Ottoman Empire.
